hot.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
hot.summary: The authors compare multimodal model designs by separating visual pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and where image processing occurs, while controlling data and compute. At the longest budget for a 1.7B backbone, in-fusion reaches 49.2% Avg. VQA, versus 48.9% for a scratch encoder and 44.8% without dedicated vision processing. These dense-backbone experiments do not rule out benefits from external data.

hot.title: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier: Scaling Law for Latent Feedback Transformers on Repeated Data
hot.summary: The authors test latent feedback, which passes each token’s top-layer state into the next token’s input, against a repeated-data Transformer. At matched validation loss, it uses 48% less compute (60M, 400 UTPP, two epochs) and 41% less unique data (271M, 100 UTPP, three epochs). It can lose when data is scarce; evidence covers one recipe, dataset and model ladder.

hot.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
hot.summary: Ropedia Xperience 2 pairs metric-scale scans with head-mounted task recordings, registering them to a shared spatial frame for robot-learning reuse. Its released scan component has 1,589 scans; the broader inventory includes 596 locations, 4,230 recordings, 74 tasks, and 131 hours. In simulation, one eight-subtask task succeeded from all 30 held-out starts; this single result does not establish broad or physical-robot performance.

hot.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
hot.summary: PixVid adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to generate pixels one frame at a time, replacing temporally compressed VAE latents with pixel patches. It predicts clean video and aligns controls to individual frames, avoiding block waits. On text-to-video generation, it scores 84.78 VBench versus 84.05 for Wan2.1, while control latency falls from 495 ms to 34 ms at lower throughput.

hot.title: An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning
hot.summary: The tutorial presents energy-based models as a framework for understanding and composing machine-learning methods. Each method is described through its energy representation, inference procedure, and learning process; adding energy terms can combine requirements and reuse separately learned components. Examples in planning and toy sampling illustrate this approach, but do not establish reliable composition or generalization in arbitrary tasks.

hot.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
hot.summary: JEV uses one fixed decision model as Actor, Judge, and Teacher: it scores rollout actions after the trajectory, and centered scores augment GRPO outcome advantages during training. For Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Hindsight + Progress raises ALFWorld All success from 72.8% ± 3.6 to 82.9% ± 2.9, and WebShop success from 56.8% ± 3.8 to 71.4% ± 0.7, in two text environments with episodes capped at 30 and 15 actions, respectively.

hot.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
hot.summary: SALA connects separately recorded human and robot videos through atomic-action descriptions, using graded semantic relationships to align human-video latents with robot latents grounded by robot-action reconstruction. Its policy learns from both video types with one action expert. On a 63-DoF robot, 2,678 hours of human-video pre-training reduced held-out action error by 2.21% versus none; increasing human demonstrations raised success by 18.75 percentage points in these tests.

hot.title: Beyond the Training Distribution: A Survey of Reasoning Generalization in Large Language Models
hot.summary: The authors survey how large language models generalize reasoning procedures across explicit distribution shifts. They organize methods by whether they act during training, inference, or architecture, and review behavioral, mechanistic, and theoretical evidence. The survey finds that methods can help in particular settings, but none consistently generalizes across shifts; differences among studies preclude controlled comparisons.

hot.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
hot.summary: Singularity-Bench evaluates whether coding agents can build systems across the artificial-intelligence development stack. It tests six tasks spanning training, serving, agent harnesses, and cluster management, comparing systems with mature references on identical hardware. Its equal-weight index reports Opus 5.5 with Claude Code matching or exceeding references across all six tasks, scoring 1.252; this is a proxy, not full recursive self-improvement.

hot.title: Interpretable Weight-Space Programming Builds Transparent Transformers and Brain Encoding Models
hot.summary: iWSP lets a coding agent write interpretable model features directly and revise them using a fixed evaluator’s score, rather than learning feature weights through backpropagation. In brain encoding, the evaluator fits ridge-regression readouts. The visual model outperforms interpretable baselines on held-out data in early and ventral cortex, but trails AlexNet in ventral cortex; story-position features also reveal scan-edge timing.

hot.title: ACE-CaP-0: Real-World Code-as-Policies in the Era of Experience
hot.summary: ACE-CaP-0 develops task-specific robot programs by using demonstrations, simulation, and physical trials to revise candidate code. Its frozen programs use runtime perception but run without a human or coding agent choosing each action. Across eight tasks, they succeed in 221 of 240 real-world trials (92.1%); this is pooled performance across separate task programs, not one general-purpose policy.

hot.title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
hot.summary: ArchSpace proposes a workflow for recording and testing language-model architecture ideas against baselines in staged experiments. Its coupled scaling law models loss across model size and training tokens, with a term for learning-rate and batch-size choices, and predicts loss on four frozen-law extrapolation runs with 0.32% MAPE. This supports screening under tested conditions, not skipping tests or proving architecture gains.

hot.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
hot.summary: UGG unifies video generation and geometric prediction by completing aligned RGB, depth, and camera-ray representations from observed scene components. A shared multimodal model treats observed tokens as context and denoises missing ones; test-time search ranks candidate completions using image-derived evidence. On RealEstate10K with only endpoint images, search lowers translation-direction angular error from 8.260° to 3.475°, but verification is imperfect.

hot.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
hot.summary: FOAM reduces SOAP’s cost by retaining input-side preconditioning and summarizing rotated second moments with row and column means. In GPT-2 large (760M) FineWeb pre-training, FOAM’s final validation loss was 2.796 ± 0.005 nats, close to SOAP’s 2.791 ± 0.005. It reached AdamW’s final-loss target in 10.53 hours versus SOAP’s 22.66, using 11.87 versus 23.73 GiB of matrix-parameter state; evidence is limited to GPT-2-scale models.

hot.title: Knowledge Distillation for Language Models: A Survey of Training Contexts and Supervision
hot.summary: The survey classifies knowledge distillation by training-context origin and, for student-generated contexts, by whether the generating checkpoint is current or earlier. It separates context provenance from teacher supervision and applies the framework across generation, embeddings, retrieval, and agents. A reported Lightning OPD 8B setup uses 30 rather than 120 GPU-hours, but this does not test the taxonomy experimentally.

hot.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
hot.summary: PhysLoop uses executable simulations to construct and check physical events, then refines videos for training examples or localized repair. It verifies simulated motion against task conditions and checks refined outputs, with feedback guiding revisions. On a 50-task repair evaluation, the full system achieves 86.00% success versus 19.33% for standalone Seedance 2.5. This is task-specific performance, not proof of real-world physical accuracy.

hot.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
hot.summary: The authors identify sparse attention heads that encode an upcoming coding subgoal and use GoalScope to turn their activations into a description of the next action. Redirecting these heads to another task specification switches the model to that task’s subgoal, including across programming languages. The evidence concerns prompted coding tasks, not robust obstacle persistence or goals in a broader sense.

hot.title: A Survey on Human–AI Alignment: Taxonomy, Methods, and Challenges
hot.summary: The authors present a lifecycle framework for human–AI alignment, connecting specification, supervision, mechanisms, and assurance. It traces how desired behavior is defined, evidenced, shaped during training or inference, and tested under changed conditions, with findings feeding back to earlier stages. The survey finds benchmark accuracy alone does not establish PPO usefulness, based on an observational comparison.

hot.title: A Survey on Knowledge Distillation of Vision-Language Models
hot.summary: The authors survey knowledge distillation for vision-language models, organizing methods by transferred knowledge, teacher access, and structural compatibility. They explain why matching outputs may not align representations, and find that methods combining response and feature supervision score better in comparisons. On GQA, Switch-KD scores 63.9 versus 58.7 for LLaVA-MoD; confounds limit conclusions, and grounding-fidelity evaluation is lacking.

hot.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
hot.summary: CRAM (Compact Reasoning Associative Memory) learns a pairwise energy over candidate puzzle boards and searches for low-energy solutions rather than repeatedly predicting digits. It guides cell-by-cell search while keeping clues fixed. It solves 99.996% of 412,786 Sudoku-Extreme test puzzles, with 282-fold fewer inference FLOPs than EBR at matched accuracy; these structured-puzzle results do not establish general reasoning ability.

likes.title: A Survey on Continuous Diffusion and Flow Language Models
likes.summary: The authors survey continuous language models for parallel, few-step text generation, explaining how shared sequence flows couple token positions and how learned flow maps make finite jumps. They contrast this with independent marginal sampling and discuss RePlaid’s training-compute gap: 20× with self-conditioning, down from Plaid’s 64×. Scaling matched discrete diffusion over the evaluated compute range; practical efficiency remains open.

likes.title: FlashStates: Unlocking Flexible Hybrid State Management for Agentic LLM Inference
likes.summary: FlashStates improves prefix reuse for hybrid language models, which require both attention key-value tensors and a recurrent checkpoint at the same prefix endpoint. Arbitrary State Checkpointing captures that complete state at request endpoints, while a cost-aware policy jointly admits and evicts states. On GLM-5.3-Flash, it delivers 4.66 million prefill tokens per minute per GPU, 3.14× vLLM, in coding-agent trace replays on three hybrid models, not a universal serving guarantee.

likes.title: Embodied First Exam
likes.summary: The Embodied First Exam (EFE) evaluates coding agents controlling robots across direct control, controller-writing, and policy-training approaches. It standardizes tasks, information access, resources, and external verification across 1,156 tasks, 35 suites, and 47 robots. On 391 paired core tasks, GPT-6 Astra solved 30% in Standard and 77% in Privileged; these simulated results compare access conditions, not real-world readiness.

likes.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
likes.summary: Evolving Infra adapts prefill–decode allocation and KV-cache management to changing agent workloads. Nodes switch phases while cached state remains accessible, and the router uses workload estimates and branches to place requests. In a Kimi K2.6 replay on 36 GB300 GPUs, mean end-to-end latency was 38.7 seconds versus 51.5 for the best static split; the result is specific to the setup.

likes.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
likes.summary: The authors present Sage-Taiyi, a research system that tracks evidence, assumptions, uncertainty, and scope to guide which targets and reasoning methods to pursue. In expert-guided cobalt-catalyzed carbonylation, condition optimization raised isolated yield from trace to 84%. On Taiyi-Bench, Sage-Taiyi scored 53.95 versus 47.85 for AI Scientist-v2; this full-system comparison does not isolate monitoring’s contribution.

likes.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
likes.summary: Deletion Tuning learns masks that zero selected gate-projection weights while keeping the pretrained model frozen. It uses trainable logits initialized from Wanda scores, rather than learning replacement values. On Qwen3-30B-A3B, it reaches 58.54% versus full fine-tuning’s 58.43% on the SimpleRL-Zoo mean, with a 29.6-MB adapter versus 116,471-MB. Retention evidence is limited to GRPO runs on three Llama sizes.

likes.title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
likes.summary: Agency inserts an interposition layer between harnesses, models, and tools to reduce context and calls. Its techniques compact context, remove stale history, search metadata, and batch calls. Across 200 tasks, four models, and three harnesses, they average 0.77 of baseline cost and 0.97 of baseline accuracy, though some tasks cost more and accuracy declines on some OfficeQA tasks.

likes.title: Speculative Self-Distillation enables Efficient Knowledge Internalization
likes.summary: The paper introduces selective self-distillation (SSD), training a model to answer using context-informed teacher guidance. SSD uses the teacher’s next token when its prediction differs from the student’s beyond a threshold, while applying distillation loss at every response position. Across three QA tasks, it uses 38–69% fewer supervised tokens than on-policy training, with accuracy within 1.4 percentage points except on Company Memo.

likes.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
likes.summary: The authors introduce Approximate Policy Mirror Descent (APMD), which repeatedly resets the KL-regularization reference to the latest policy and makes strongly regularized local updates. They define response coverage as the average reciprocal probability of generating an optimal response. In a constructed bandit, REINFORCE needs exponentially many gradient steps, while stylized PPO-NoClip has a polynomial bound under softmax-linear policies and linear rewards.

likes.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
likes.summary: Evolving Infra adapts prefill–decode allocation for agent workloads while keeping KV cache state available across nodes as roles change. Its planner estimates phase workloads, while routing and eviction manage reusable cache. On a shifting Kimi K2.6 workload, mean end-to-end request latency was 38.7 seconds, versus 83.1 with Dynamo. P95 TTFT rose above Dynamo on decode-heavy Putnam at two tested concurrency levels.

likes.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
likes.summary: SimplEvo lets embodied agents retain task guidance and lessons from their attempts in two text memories, without changing model weights or delegating execution to a controller. Memories are learned during training and fixed at test time. In simulation, success rate reaches 81.7% on EBench, up from 46.7% under direct control; evidence is limited to two simulated benchmarks, not physical robots.

likes.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
likes.summary: The authors introduce LingBot-Touch, which maps different tactile sensors’ readings into a shared representation of contact that robot policies can reuse. Its frozen encoder supplies features alongside policy inputs. Across 26 real-robot tasks, adding these features to LingBot-VLA raises mean success from 48.3% to 73.1%, versus 56.5% with raw touch; gains are not universal, and evaluation covers two hands and fingertip-focused data.

likes.title: The Minimum Canonical Volume of Threefolds of General Type
likes.summary: The authors prove that smooth complex projective threefolds of general type have canonical volume at least 1/420. They use restrictions of holomorphic two-forms to divisors and whole pluricanonical members, plus numerical tests, to exclude the remaining cases with Euler characteristics two and three. A smooth model of a general degree-46 hypersurface in P(4,5,6,7,23) attains the bound.

likes.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
likes.summary: WorldFoundry defines a world model by a loop in which a system maintains state from interaction history, predicts action effects, and revises state from new observations, then provides contracts for running and evaluating systems while preserving native semantics. Its catalog lists 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 metric entries; one OpenVLA task succeeds in 179 steps, while two reach 520-step limits.
